title: The Independent Designer’s Research Department
author: RN Collins
principle: Evidence leads; atmosphere never substitutes for provenance.

narrativeSequence.caption: An independent designer can operate a rigorous research department by making questions, sources, permissions, interpretation, counterevidence, and retrieval part of the studio rhythm.
A less-remembered house remains researchable because its object record survives.

01 · ASK — Can the question change the work?. Frame a bounded design or institutional question, a decision date, relevant communities, and evidence that would require revision. “Inspiration” is too broad to audit.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 02 · SOURCE — Can each reference be recovered?. Preserve creator, title, date, institution, identifier, canonical URL, access date, rights statement, excerpt limits, and local notes. Keep link-only records visible without copying restricted media.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 03 · INTERPRET — Where does fact end and judgment begin?. Write source description, studio inference, transformation, disagreement, and cultural-authority question in separate fields. This prevents an appealing object from being made to prove more than its record supports.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

narrativeSequence.caption: 04 · RETURN — What did research change?. Attach the altered silhouette, material, process, refusal, claim, credit, or archive rule to the source trail. If nothing changed, record why the reference was rejected rather than laundering it into a mood board.
narrativeSequence.rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery
